text.p: These are the main stories in Latvian newspapers on Friday. Prepared for Reuters by the Cooperation Fund. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- Lithuanian President Algirdas Brazauskas confirmed that he would participate at the meeting of the three Baltic presidents in Riga, scheduled for November 26.

- The Latvian foreign ministry called in Lithuanian Ambassador Rymantas Karazija to express its incomprehension over statements by Lithuanian officials about the publication in Lithuania's Verslo Zinios newspaper of reportedly insulting remarks by Latvian Prime Minister Andris Shkele about Lithuanian officials.
- Some 200 disabled people, including children, held a picket near the government buildings to protest against new cabinet regulations abolishing free bus and railway tickets for disabled people.
- The head of the Department of Prisons, Stanislav Poksan, has been temporarily suspended pending an investigation into his activities.

- Supporters of the mayor of the eastern town of Daugavpils, Aleksey Vidavski, have collected 13,490 signatures and sent a letter to President Guntis Ulmanis asking him to revise the law on local elections, which would ban Vidavski and other people who were in the Communist Party after January 13 1991 from running in the next local elections.
- Parliament postponed the law on the privatisation of land in rural areas but Shkele wants to call an extraordinary sessioin to consider the bill before then.
- A new ferry service between Riga and Stockholm will start on November 27.
